cards.prompt: Make the random draws below reproducible.
cards.explain: `set.seed()` fixes where R's random-number generator starts, once, at the top of the script.
A die can land on the same face twice, so draw with replacement.

cards.prompt: The proportion of scores above 130 when the mean is 100 and the SD 15.
cards.explain: `pnorm()` gives the area below; `lower.tail = FALSE` gives the area above (about .023).
`qnorm()` turns a proportion into a score: 97.5% of the standard normal lies below 1.96.

cards.prompt: Simulate 1,000 ages from a normal model with mean 40 and SD 5.
cards.explain: `rnorm(n, mean, sd)` draws n random values from a normal curve.

cards.prompt: The means of 1,000 random crews of 30.
cards.explain: `replicate(n, expr)` runs the expression n times and keeps each result.

cards.prompt: You quadruple the sample size. What happens to the standard error of the mean?
Which shrinks as you recruit more participants?
cards.explain: The SD describes the spread of the data and settles near σ. The SE describes the precision of the mean and shrinks with √n.
